**Claim.** Yes. The topology induced by $d'$ coincides with the product topology on $\prod_{i\in\mathbb N} X_i$ (assuming each $(X_i, d_i)$ is a metric space).

We first note $d'$ is a genuine metric. Non-negativity and symmetry are immediate. For the triangle inequality, the key sub-inequality is
$$\min\{a+b,\,1\}\;\le\;\\min\{a,1\}+\min\{b,1\},\qquad a,b\ge 0,$$
which holds because: if $a+b\le 1$ the left side is $a+b$ and the right side is $\ge a+b$; if $a+b>1$ the left side is $1$, while the right side is $\ge 1$ (if both $a,b<1$ it equals $a+b>1$; if $a\ge 1$ it is $\ge 1$). Applying this coordinatewise with $a=d_i(x_i,y_i)$, $b=d_i(y_i,z_i)$ and summing with weights $2^{-i}$ gives $d'(x,z)\le d'(x,y)+d'(y,z)$. Finally $d'(x,y)=0$ forces every $\min\{d_i(x_i,y_i),1\}=0$, hence $x_i=y_i$ for all $i$, so $x=y$.

We now prove the two topologies are equal by showing each contains the other.

---

**Part 1. Every $d'$-open set is product-open.**

It suffices to show: for every $x_0$ and $r>0$, each $x\in B_{d'}(x_0,r)$ has a product-neighborhood contained in $B_{d'}(x_0,r)$.

Let $x\in B_{d'}(x_0,r)$ and set $s=d'(x_0,x)<r$, $\varepsilon=r-s>0$. Choose $N$ so large that $\sum_{i=N+1}^{\infty}2^{-i}=2^{-N}<\varepsilon/2$. Define the basic product-open set
$$U=\prod_{i=1}^{N}B_{d_i}\!\bigl(x_i,\,\varepsilon/2\bigr)\;\times\;\prod_{i=N+1}^{\infty}X_i,$$
which contains $x$. For any $y\in U$,
$$d'(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}2^{-i}\min\{d_i(x_i,y_i),1\}+\sum_{i=N+1}^{\infty}2^{-i}\min\{d_i(x_i,y_i),1\}.$$
The first sum is $<(\varepsilon/2)\sum_{i=1}^{N}2^{-i}<\varepsilon/2$; the second is $\le\sum_{i=N+1}^{\infty}2^{-i}=2^{-N}<\varepsilon/2$. Hence $d'(x,y)<\varepsilon$, and by the triangle inequality
$$d'(x_0,y)\le d'(x_0,x)+d'(x,y)<s+\varepsilon=r.$$
So $y\in B_{d'}(x_0,r)$, giving $U\subseteq B_{d'}(x_0,r)$. Thus every $d'$-open set is product-open.

---

**Part 2. Every product-open set is $d'$-open.**

A basic open set in the product topology has the form $U=\prod_{i=1}^{N}U_i\times\prod_{i=N+1}^{\infty}X_i$ with each $U_i$ open in $X_i$ (only finitely many factors are proper). Let $x\in U$. For each $i\le N$, pick $r_i>0$ with $B_{d_i}(x_i,r_i)\subseteq U_i$. Set
$$r=\min_{1\le i\le N}\;2^{-i}\min\{r_i,1\}>0.$$
We claim $B_{d'}(x,r)\subseteq U$. Let $y\in B_{d'}(x,r)$, so $d'(x,y)<r$. For each $i\le N$,
$$2^{-i}\min\{d_i(x_i,y_i),1\}\;\le\;d'(x,y)\;<\;r\;\le\;2^{-i}\min\{r_i,1\},$$
hence $\min\{d_i(x_i,y_i),1\}<\min\{r_i,1\}$.

- If $r_i\le 1$: this reads $\min\{d_i(x_i,y_i),1\}<r_i\le 1$, forcing $d_i(x_i,y_i)<r_i$.
- If $r_i>1$: this reads $\min\{d_i(x_i,y_i),1\}<1$, forcing $d_i(x_i,y_i)<1<r_i$.

In either case $y_i\in B_{d_i}(x_i,r_i)\subseteq U_i$. For $i>N$ we have $y_i\in X_i$ trivially. Therefore $y\in U$, proving $B_{d'}(x,r)\subseteq U$.

So every basic product-open set is $d'$-open, hence every product-open set is $d'$-open.

---

**Conclusion.** Part 1 gives $\tau_{d'}\subseteq\tau_{\text{prod}}$ and Part 2 gives $\tau_{\text{prod}}\subseteq\tau_{d'}$. Therefore the topology induced by $d'$ coincides exactly with the product topology on $\prod_{i\in\mathbb N}X_i$. $\blacksquare$
